boom.name: Boom
boom.blurb: Markets are cheerful and companies are hiring.

slowdown.name: Slowdown
slowdown.blurb: Growth cools, hiring freezes and raises shrink.

crisis.name: Crisis
crisis.blurb: Markets crash, jobs get shaky and prices still rise.

provenance.basis: Illustrative four-state economy, tuned so the long-run mix is about 23% boom, 50% steady, 18% slowdown, 10% crisis. Inflation per regime averages about 4.5% across the mix (boom 5.1, steady 4.3, slowdown 3.8, crisis 5.3), so prices rise about 5.3 times over 38 years. It was 5.2% until the November 2026 review: that matched the 2012-2026 CPI average of about 5.6% but looked high for a 60-year view. 4.5% sits between the RBI's 4% target (band 2-6%) and the 4.9% average of the targeting era; recent years were lower (RBI put FY2025-26 near 2.1%) and FY2026-27 is projected near 5%. Sources are secondary summaries (RBI, Trading Economics, press), not checked against MoSPI. Crises last about 1.7 years on average. wageAdjPct is the extra raise (in percentage points) a fully cyclical job gets that year, averaging about zero across the mix.
